# About me 

::: grid
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-lg-6}


***`I`m quite interested*** in different aspects of political economy and economic history, particularly regarding economic inequalities. 

I first got in contact with economics through the [works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_in_the_Twenty-First_Century) of Thomas Piketty (not very original, I admit), but was quite quickly disappointed with the way it was taught at my university. Subsequently, I joined [Rethinking Economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rethinking_Economics), which played a significant role in shaping my economic understanding. 

After a stop at the [UN in NYC](https://policy.desa.un.org/) and at  [some](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halle_Institute_for_Economic_Research) [research](https://iw.wiwi.uni-halle.de/?lang=en) [institutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leibniz_Institute_of_Agricultural_Development_in_Transition_Economies) in Germany, I am now studying [Economics with a focus on Development](https://psme.pantheonsorbonne.fr/) at Panthéon-Sorbonne in Paris.

On this website I collect various projects and ideas, adorned with a bunch of  Vermeer paintings (like the one on this page: [The Geographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Geographer) )
